name: Victor Novak

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions or government, and your answers are confidential. What does an ordinary workday look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 58 and have managed nine school-book account staff for a large publisher for years. We plan reprints, answer schools when an edition is wrong and make sure a promised shipment is actually at the warehouse. I have a bachelor’s degree and am about average among the managers here. I use an approved AI demand forecast now and then after our planners have checked it, but I still ask the warehouse whether the cartons contain the current edition.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner is a hospital receptionist, and our grown children live in their own homes. We have a small mortgage and about four months of expenses saved. I receive typical manager pay and can see some similar supply offices nearby. Retirement is coming closer, but we have not checked an actual income statement or when it could be paid. My partner’s wage is steady; neither of us wants a school paying twice for the wrong books.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the staff AI Plateau may help forecast another print run, but a school needs the right edition in its boxes. I would keep the warehouse count and the teacher’s order beside any software estimate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think my experienced account role will stay if the tool only saves some checking time. Four months saved and my partner’s regular receptionist wage make the mortgage manageable. I would not change jobs over a small improvement in forecasting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep our weekly call with the warehouse and compare edition codes before confirming school orders. I would continue using the approved forecast only when the planners have checked it, then verify the actual cartons. If the mild change arrives in 2027, I would keep the call and make our normal mortgage payments.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about my own work and bills here. I would be embarrassed to send a teacher last year’s science text under a current label.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which order caused trouble?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A school ordered thirty current science books, and our system pulled last year’s version. The warehouse worker read the code aloud before the cartons left. We corrected the pick and the class got the right diagrams.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you let the forecast place the order?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not without the warehouse confirming the edition and count. The forecast helps me see demand, but it does not open a carton. I use it now and then, not as a replacement for the people handling the books.

say: A **reprint forecast** cannot replace the right edition in school cartons.
I would match **warehouse codes** to teacher orders.
think: My **experienced role** looks steady under minor AI change.
Four months saved and **receptionist pay** support the mortgage.
do: **Keep** weekly warehouse calls and edition-code checks.
**Use** approved forecast after planner review, then verify actual cartons before confirming school orders.
feel: I feel **calm** about work but embarrassed by wrong school editions.
S0.quote: A school ordered thirty current science books, and our system pulled last year’s version.
fieldNote: His **occasional AI use** is already tied to planner and warehouse verification.
A **four-month reserve** and regular receptionist wage support calm under modest change while mortgage payments still matter.

steps.text: Keep weekly warehouse calls before confirming school orders
Use approved forecast only with planner and actual carton checks

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues stronger AI could predict reprints and write school replies, so the company may cut account jobs. I would show the number of corrected orders and teacher complaints alongside software savings. A box delivered fast with the wrong edition is still a failure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think one manager could oversee more school accounts, and my post might be among those combined. I know our schools and suppliers, but much of my reporting can be generated. Four months saved lets us search for a while, not live without my wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next month I would bring the wrong-edition cases to the staff union and ask for written staffing plans. I would make a list of posted local educational-supply roles, but apply only when a real vacancy shows net pay after travel that covers our mortgage and bills; I would accept only a confirmed offer with hours we can manage. I would keep the warehouse calls while still employed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about being absorbed into a larger account team. The teacher waiting for a current diagram is why I would argue for checking cartons, not just headcount.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you show the union?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The original school order, the edition packed and the cost of collecting a wrong box. One returned science set needed a second van trip during exam week. A fast email apology did not put the right diagram on a desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would a supply role be safer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It would still involve orders and reports, so strong AI could change it too. I would treat a local posting as an option only if the pay and hours work. I would not call it a rescue job.

say: **Forecast automation** may reduce school account jobs even when teachers still need a person to correct the wrong edition.
I would publish **corrected orders** and teacher complaints beside savings.
think: A wider team could absorb my **manager post**.
Four months saved cannot replace my **wage** for a long search.
do: **Bring** wrong-edition cases to union next month for staffing terms.
**Apply** only to posted supply roles with net pay after travel covering mortgage and bills.
feel: I feel **anxious** about consolidation and protective of school orders.
S1.quote: A fast email apology did not put the right diagram on a desk.
fieldNote: He uses **teacher evidence** and union channels rather than promising school-supply desks remain safe.
A **local vacancy** needs actual bill-covering net pay, manageable hours and a confirmed offer.

steps.text: Bring wrong-edition cases to union for written staffing plans
Apply to posted supply roles only with mortgage-and-bill net pay after travel
Accept only confirmed offer after checking actual hours
Keep warehouse edition checks while employed

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the company AGI by 2028 could order reprints and answer schools before anyone has agreed who corrects a wrong edition. The union should have notice terms and a person with authority to stop a bad shipment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I fear our account office could be cut quickly, and my own role might go. Other supply offices also plan and write, so they face 2028 AGI. Packing books remains physical until capable robots around 2031, but I cannot assume a warehouse vacancy or a manager wage there. Four months saved keeps us from immediate trouble, not from needing income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I would ask the union for written severance and a stop-shipment rule. I would review the mortgage and four-month reserve with my partner, using our two actual wages rather than counting any future school contract. If AGI arrives in 2028 and my role ends, I would apply to advertised local account or warehouse-support work only with verified pay after travel that covers the mortgage and bills; I would accept only an actual offer with workable hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing a team I know. I have a short search window and some offices nearby, but a warehouse role is not waiting with my name on it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a stop-shipment rule do?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A warehouse worker sees the old edition code and can hold the pallet before the lorry leaves. An AI reply after a class opens the wrong book is too late to help that lesson. I want the person with the carton to have the authority to stop it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you work in the warehouse?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would check a real posting and the physical demands first. I have visited the floor but have not worked full packing shifts for years. Robots for hands-on packing come around 2031 in this picture, so it is not a permanent refuge.

say: **2028 AGI** needs notice and authority to hold a wrong edition.
I would seek written **severance terms** for account staff.
think: My **own account post** might go in rapid cuts.
Other supply desks face **2028 AGI**, while physical packing robots follow around 2031.
do: **Ask** union this week for severance and stop-shipment rules.
**Review** mortgage and reserve against both actual household wages.
**Apply** after a 2028 loss only to advertised roles with mortgage-and-bill pay after travel and workable hours.
feel: I feel **anxious** about team loss despite some search time.
S2.quote: An AI reply after a class opens the wrong book is too late to help that lesson.
fieldNote: His **moderate reserve** and local options support a short search, not an assumed warehouse job.
He distinguishes **2028 supply-desk exposure** from physical packing robots around 2031.

steps.text: Ask union for written severance and old-edition stop-shipment authority
Apply after loss to advertised roles with mortgage-and-bill pay after travel
Accept only confirmed offer with checked hours and physical duties

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years is time to put edition checks in the contract and name who can stop a wrong pallet. I would also want schools to know whether a promised reprint is actually funded, rather than being shown a beautiful forecast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I can build a better account record before 2031, but the planning and reply work I do still faces AGI that year. Physical warehouse packing meets capable robots around 2034. At 63 I do not know whether any retirement payment would be enough, and I would not make a physical job plan without checking its wage and demands.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2027 I would ask the warehouse lead for a paid half-day each quarter reviewing edition errors; I would attend only if my director approves account cover and the lead agrees to check my work. I would ask local supply firms for their posted pay ranges, then apply only to a real role with net wages after travel covering our mortgage and bills. After 2031 I would accept only a confirmed offer whose duties and hours I can manage, while keeping the current school accounts as long as real work remains.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my desk, but five years lets me learn where the errors begin. A half-day looking at cartons would not make me a warehouse supervisor.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the lead show you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The print date, edition code and pick sheet for a returned pallet. I can read the customer order, but I have not been responsible for a full packing shift. The lead would have to tell me when my account note missed a real floor problem.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would a half-day earn a new role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. It would improve the job I have and show me what a floor role really requires. I would still need a posted vacancy with adequate wage and duties I can do.

say: A **five-year runway** should bring funded reprints and clear stop-pallet authority.
I would show schools **real print funding**, not a forecast alone.
think: School-account planning faces **2031 AGI**, with physical packing robots around 2034.
At **63**, retirement pay and a floor role’s physical demands remain uncertain.
do: **Request** quarterly paid edition reviews; attend only with director-approved cover and warehouse-lead checking.
**Ask** supply firms for posted wage ranges before applying.
**Apply** to real supply roles only with mortgage-and-bill net pay after travel and manageable duties.
feel: I feel **anxious** about desk exposure but able to inspect real errors.
S3.quote: A half-day looking at cartons would not make me a warehouse supervisor.
fieldNote: His **warehouse visit** is paid learning for current accounts, not a claim of a new trade.
A **supply job** still requires a posted vacancy, mortgage-and-bill net pay and manageable work.

steps.text: Apply for posted supply role only with mortgage-and-bill net pay after travel and manageable duties
Accept only confirmed offer with workable hours and duties

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the union a decade is enough to write a worker’s stop-shipment right and give staff a true account of print funding. A school should not discover at the start of term that the right edition exists only in a forecast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I will be 68 by 2036. I might want to stop working then, but I have not checked actual retirement eligibility or net income. Our four-month reserve is useful but not a pension. School-account reports face 2036 AGI, while physical packing meets robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep the warehouse code checks and request a verified retirement-income statement, comparing income plus savings with mortgage and bills. I would add fifty to our reserve only after both wages arrive in full and the mortgage and utilities clear. After 2036 I would keep paid work if verified retirement income plus savings cannot meet those bills, and apply to a posted local role if the publisher no longer has real account work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about an unverified retirement amount and a job that may end. Ten years gives room to save a little, but it does not make a promised edition appear on a shelf.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your children contribute to retirement?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They have their own households and costs. We would tell them if we were in trouble, but we would not write their wages into our plan. I want a statement and a bill list that belong to us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why just fifty extra?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The mortgage is still due and we will not empty the four months already saved. Fifty from two full wages after bills is a real addition. If the hospital cuts my partner’s receptionist hours, the extra transfer waits.

say: A **decade** should bring a stop-shipment right and honest print funding.
I would not call a **forecast edition** a delivered school book.
think: At **68**, retirement entitlement and net income remain unverified.
School-account reports face **2036 AGI**, with physical packing robots around 2039.
do: **Save** fifty extra only after both full wages, mortgage and utilities clear.
**Continue** paid work after 2036 if verified retirement income plus savings cannot meet bills.
feel: I feel **anxious** about the desk and unknown retirement amount.
S4.quote: A school should not discover at the start of term that the right edition exists only in a forecast.
fieldNote: His **fifty transfer** adds newly earned money after both full wages and mortgage costs.
He does not assume **retirement entitlement** or grown-child funding without real figures.

steps.text: Keep checking edition codes with warehouse before confirming school orders
Save fifty only after both full wages mortgage and utilities clear
Continue paid work after 2036 if verified income plus savings cannot meet bills
Apply to posted local role if real publisher account work ends

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. The school-account office could shrink before a real job with our mortgage wage appears. Written notice, a warehouse stop-shipment right and a posted role with enough pay would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the teacher to open the carton before calling the shipment complete. Thirty books with last year’s diagrams are not thirty useful books. I would rather correct the order than celebrate a fast delivery.

headlineQuote: Thirty books with last year’s diagrams are not thirty useful books.
portrait: **Victor, 58**, is an experienced school-book account manager supervising nine staff at a large publisher.
His **typical pay**, receptionist partner, four-month reserve and some local supply offices support a small mortgage.
He uses **AI occasionally** for demand forecasts, then checks actual edition codes and cartons.
He is **calm** under mild change and anxious about his exposed account post and unverified retirement income.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could shrink his school-account role before a mortgage-paying alternative appears.
whatWouldHelp: Written **notice**, stop-shipment authority and a real posted role with enough pay would help.
